subject: Clarify: ephemeral snapshot slicing, custody, and deletion windows after incident
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@deltahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@deltahealth.com
Date: 2026-04-18T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious activity follow-up — snapshot exports

Mina, thanks for the quick call earlier. We noticed a set of ephemeral VM snapshots created around 04/17 22:10 UTC that look relevant to the event. Our compliance team needs to confirm: what is Redwood's retention policy for ephemeral snapshot artifacts created during transient jobs? Specifically: 1) how long are snapshot diffs kept by default, 2) do you slice or dedupe snapshots across instances before archival, and 3) if we request deletion, what is the expected time-to-delete and verification proof? Attachments: snapshot-ids.csv (list of snapshot IDs we see).

Can you confirm custody and deletion steps so we can update our internal evidence timeline?

— Alex
Security Operations, DeltaHealth
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@deltahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious activity follow-up — snapshot exports

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for including the CSV. Short answers up front:
- Default retention for ephemeral snapshot diffs generated during inference jobs: 14 days.
- We apply snapshot slicing + dedup during archival: identical blocks across snapshots are deduped and we keep a manifest that maps snapshot IDs to stored chunks.
- On customer-initiated deletion requests we perform logical deletion within 48 hours and physical purge of deduped chunks within 7 days, with a verification report once complete.

Notes / caveats:
- The 14-day window is configurable per tenant for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers get the 14-day default unless SLA specifies otherwise.
- If a snapshot is part of an active forensics hold or legal hold (initiated by either Redwood or the customer), deletion is suspended until the hold is lifted.

Next steps: can you flag which snapshot IDs in your CSV you want put on a hold vs. scheduled for deletion? I will loop in Karthik for chain-of-custody docs and Marissa for any formal evidence transfer.

Attachments: forensic-checklist.pdf (internal checklist we use to preserve chain-of-custody).

— Mina
Sr. Incident Response Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Alex Green <alex.green@deltahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious activity follow-up — snapshot exports

Alex / Mina — plumbing details from custody side:
- When we receive a hold request we create a hold ticket and tag the snapshot manifest; the manifest and associated chunk references are exported to an immutable escrow bundle if the customer requests escrow. Escrow creation typically takes 4–8 hours for a small set (~10–50 snapshots), longer for bulk.
- Proof-of-deletion: after logical deletion we generate a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 of the prior manifest + timestamp) and push to the customer shared Drive link; after physical purge we provide a second signed confirmation.
- Sampling and slicing policy: if DeltaHealth requests a subset for rapid review we can produce a sliced export (time-window + instance IDs): sliced exports include a minimal set of deduped chunks plus the mapping file so you can rehydrate the snapshot locally. Sliced exports are kept in a locked bucket for 30 days by default.

Question: Alex, do you need the escrow bundle now or just the hold + deletion plan? If escrow is required we will initiate the export and coordinate secure transfer keys with your team.

— Karthik
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference
